FFmpeg in JeffDeck
==================

What it is
----------
JeffDeck plays the movies and sounds in a presentation through Qt Multimedia.
Qt Multimedia's FFmpeg backend reads and decodes the files with FFmpeg's
libraries, which come with the program:

  libavcodec, libavformat, libavutil, libswresample, and libswscale
  (on Windows avcodec-*.dll and its kin; on macOS and Linux libavcodec and its
  kin, with Qt's FFmpeg plugin, plugins/multimedia/ffmpegmediaplugin)

They are FFmpeg 7.1.5 (6.1.6 in the snap), built by JeffOffice from the official source release
with only the parts that a movie or sound in a presentation needs (see "What
is in the build," below): a build under the GNU Lesser General Public
License, version 2.1 or later (the libraries say so themselves: "libavcodec
license: LGPL version 2.1 or later"). It holds no GPL or non-free parts.
JeffDeck links to them as shared libraries, and has not changed FFmpeg's
source. JeffPub does not use them.

What is in the build
--------------------
Of FFmpeg's hundreds of file readers and decoders, the build has the ones for
the movies and sounds a presentation holds: the MP4, QuickTime, 3GP, Matroska,
WebM, AVI, ASF (Windows Media), MPEG program and transport stream, WAV, MP3,
AAC, FLAC, Ogg, and AIFF containers, and decoders for H.264, HEVC, MPEG-4,
H.263, MPEG-1, MPEG-2, Windows Media video, VC-1, VP8, VP9, Motion JPEG, raw
video, Cinepak and other older AVI video, AAC, AC-3, MP3, MP2, Windows Media
audio (also Pro and lossless), FLAC, Vorbis, Opus, ALAC, PCM, and ADPCM.
It has no encoders, no muxers, no network or playlist readers, no devices, and
no hardware decoders. The only other library is zlib (the system's, or on
Windows a static copy), by Jean-loup Gailly and Mark Adler under the zlib
License, which opens compressed movie headers and compressed Matroska tracks.
On a Mac the build also uses the system's VideoToolbox framework (only its
device type, not its hardware decoders), which comes with macOS.
The complete list is in third_party/ffmpeg-components.txt in the source, and
tools/check_ffmpeg_components.py fails the build if a component outside the
list is added, also from a probe of the built libraries themselves. A file in
another format is not played: JeffDeck says that it can't be played.

FFmpeg is a trademark of Fabrice Bellard, originator of the FFmpeg project.
JeffOffice is not connected to the FFmpeg project.

The license
-----------
The text of the GNU Lesser General Public License, version 2.1, is in
LGPL-2.1.txt, beside this file. You may use, copy, and share FFmpeg's
libraries under it. You may replace the copies that come with JeffDeck with
other builds of the same libraries (FFmpeg 7.1, the same version numbers),
and JeffDeck will use them. tools/build_ffmpeg.sh in the source makes ours.

Where the source is
-------------------
- FFmpeg 7.1.5 (6.1.6 in the snap), the file ffmpeg-7.1.5.tar.xz: https://ffmpeg.org/releases/ and
  https://git.ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg.git (the release tag n7.1.5). tools/build_ffmpeg.sh
  in the JeffOffice source downloads it, checks its SHA-256, and builds it.
- Qt Multimedia's FFmpeg backend, which loads the libraries: its source is at
  https://code.qt.io/cgit/qt/qtmultimedia.git (the FFmpeg backend is in
  src/plugins/multimedia/ffmpeg).

If you can't get the source from those places, ask at
https://github.com/JeffOffice/jeffoffice and we will send it.
